clue.text: See 27
One successfully putting into Manx cat disease

indicators.note: the golfer's word is placed into the shortened animal
a Manx cat famously has no tail, so the word cat loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written before its tail goes
a golfer who sinks a putt holes it, so is a holer

explanation.surface: Someone putting something into a tailless Isle of Man cat that is ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manx' tells you to dock the tail of CAT, giving CA; HOLER, a golfer who holes a putt, goes 'into' it. A Manx cat is a tailless breed from the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: An acute bacterial infection of the gut spread by dirty water, a classic deadly illness.

clue.text: Bit that's evading the Middle East, it's reported

indicators.note: signals that the word is heard rather than seen, so its sound gives the entry

parts.note: harmony has long eluded that region: peace

explanation.surface: A wry remark about a commodity the Middle East never manages to secure.
explanation.walkthrough: The cryptic phrase describes PEACE, which sounds just like the entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A bit is a fragment or portion, the same as a small part of something.

clue.text: Treaty barring nuclear trials puts best explosive in the shade

indicators.note: the jumbled word is placed inside the colour

parts.note: tan is a light brown shade

indicators.note: the letters of best are blown apart and reassembled

explanation.surface: A treaty on nuclear tests that eclipses the best explosive available.
explanation.walkthrough: 'explosive' rearranges BEST to ESTB, which goes 'in' TAN. 'puts' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1963 agreement prohibiting atomic weapon detonations in the atmosphere is the usual name for such an accord.

clue.text: See 23
Women of two generations later

parts.note: a mother is ma
a grandmother is nana, one generation further up

explanation.surface: A remark about a mother and grandmother living together.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase gives two women from successive generations, mother and grandmother.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish for tomorrow, used in English to mean at some indefinite future time, i.e. later.

clue.text: Stop people creating hell

parts.note: to dam is to stop a flow
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: Blocking a whole people produces hell on earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternal punishment of the condemned soul, so a synonym for the infernal place.

clue.text: Leader of Africa also gatecrashing Hindu festival

indicators.note: one word barges into the middle of the other, like an uninvited guest

parts.note: a mela is a Hindu fair or festival
and means also

explanation.surface: An African leader turning up uninvited at a Hindu celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gatecrashing' is the container signal. A mela is a South Asian fair or festival, a word worth knowing for crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelson Mandela was South Africa's first black president, a celebrated African statesman.

clue.text: Doctor prints it in publication that's caustic

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are placed inside the publication

parts.note: a newspaper is a paper

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are altered

explanation.surface: A doctored item printed in a publication that's bitingly critical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a profession but is the anagram signal; 'in' places the result inside. 'that's' links the definition, here used as a noun: a caustic substance.
explanation.definitionFit: The solvent used to remove old paint is a corrosive substance, i.e. a caustic.

clue.text: See 24
Appear to drown two articles, one a water-dweller

indicators.note: the articles are submerged inside the verb

parts.note: to seem is to appear
a is the indefinite article
an is the other form of the indefinite article
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone appearing to drown a pair of things, one of them a water creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to drown' is the container signal: the articles are submerged in the verb. The 'a' before water-dweller is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea anemone is a soft-bodied marine animal living on rocks under water.

clue.text: Rock guitarist's assistant always into R&B

indicators.note: the word for always goes inside the music abbreviation

parts.note: rhythm and blues, abbreviated RB
ever means always

explanation.surface: A rock guitarist's helper who has always loved rhythm and blues.
explanation.walkthrough: EVER goes between R and B.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverberation effect added to an electric guitar's sound, a standard piece of rock kit helping the player.

clue.text: Zero rate surprisingly faster

parts.note: none means zero

indicators.note: the letters of rate are arranged in an unexpected way

explanation.surface: A zero rate, surprisingly, is quicker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faster' looks like quicker, but it is someone who fasts. 'surprisingly' turns RATE into EATER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who fasts abstains from food, so is by definition one who doesn't eat.

clue.text: Among the pride of lions, problem turning to catch gazelle's tail for some element

indicators.note: the inner group of letters sits among those of the hair word

parts.note: a lion's mane is its pride and glory

indicators.note: the reversed word grips the final letter
the word for problem is turned round

parts.note: a snag is a problem

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A lion pride tackles a problem when catching a gazelle, in some elemental way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses, 'to catch' and 'Among' each signal a container. A lion's mane is pictured as its pride, its proudest feature.
explanation.definitionFit: Manganese is a metallic chemical element, number 25.

clue.text: Great wit, one coming down coming up in the end

indicators.note: the reversed word is placed within the aim

parts.note: a goal is an end or aim

indicators.note: in a down entry the word for a diver rises, reading upward

parts.note: a diver comes down into the water

explanation.surface: A famous wit, once fallen, rises again in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' reverses because this is a down entry; 'in' sets the result inside. 'Great wit' is a famous person, not a quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Gore Vidal, the American novelist and essayist, was famed for his barbed epigrams.

clue.text: Kilimanjaro, from which to see capital city

indicators.note: the city can be seen inside the mountain's name

explanation.surface: Looking out from Kilimanjaro to view a capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The city sits within kiLIMAnjaro.
explanation.definitionFit: Lima is the capital of Peru.

clue.text: Fifty pairs of animals here, for a bird

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
Noah's ark held the animals two by two

explanation.surface: Fifty pairs of animals collected here, all for one bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A lark is a songbird such as the skylark.

clue.text: Bad wiping face having accessed bum — with this tissue?

indicators.note: the shortened word gets inside the lounging verb

parts.note: to bum around is to loll

indicators.note: the word's front letter is wiped away

parts.note: poor means bad

explanation.surface: Crude wiping of a face after touching a backside: what tissue is needed?
explanation.walkthrough: 'wiping face' removes a first letter and 'having accessed' signals the container. 'Bum' here is the verb, to laze about; loo is British slang for toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Toilet paper on a roll is a bathroom tissue; loo is British slang for toilet.

clue.text: Very quick kiss on holiday

indicators.note: in an across entry one part is placed on, after, the other

parts.note: a break is a holiday
to neck is to kiss

explanation.surface: A snog while away on a holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Breakneck speed is dangerously fast, so the word means extremely rapid.

clue.text: Married, desperately seeking lover

indicators.note: frantic disorder rearranges the letters

explanation.surface: A married person desperately looking for someone to love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seeking' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An admirer is a suitor or devotee, one who fancies another.

clue.text: Party admitting defeat producing little bit of food

indicators.note: the party lets the other word in

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, a UK political party
a rout is a heavy defeat

explanation.surface: A party conceding defeat comes up with a crumb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitting' is the container signal. Con is the standard short form for Conservative, Britain's main right-of-centre party.
explanation.definitionFit: A crouton is a small cube of fried or toasted bread put in soup or salad.

clue.text: Some turkey, last of supper gobbled by pig

indicators.note: the final letter is swallowed by the brute

parts.note: a greedy pig is a beast

indicators.note: takes just the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A greedy pig gobbling turkey, the remains of supper.
explanation.walkthrough: R from supper goes inside BEAST after B.
explanation.definitionFit: White meat cut from a turkey's chest is one portion of the bird.

clue.text: Eat more than you during dance

indicators.note: the words sit within the dance, as if happening during it

parts.note: a hop is an informal dance
over means more than
U is text-speak for you

explanation.surface: Someone eating more than you during a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' is the container signal. Hoover is a vacuum-cleaner brand used as a verb in Britain, hence a greedy eater hoovers up food.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoover up is to devour greedily, like a vacuum cleaner.

clue.text: Military leader has the first twelve hours of the week to bring riches

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.words: the first twelve hours of the week
parts.note: a.m. Mon, the morning of Monday, written AM MON

explanation.surface: A general hogging the start of the week to amass wealth.
explanation.walkthrough: The week starts on Monday; its morning is a.m. Monday, which reads AM MON.
explanation.definitionFit: Mammon is wealth personified in the Bible, money seen as a false god.

clue.text: Introduction to "Eve" as a palindrome?

parts.note: the first man greeting the first woman with a sentence reading the same both ways

explanation.surface: How the first man presented himself, in a line that reads the same backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: Famous palindrome: Adam introducing himself to Eve in Eden.
explanation.definitionFit: This well-known palindromic sentence is the imagined first greeting Adam gave in the garden.

clue.text: Upset over comrade with ego, 14 on the death of 27 1?

indicators.note: the letters are knocked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: An upset comrade's ego, and one writer's quip on another's death.
explanation.walkthrough: Gore Vidal (14) is said to have called Truman Capote's (27 1) death this.
explanation.definitionFit: Vidal's notorious sneer at his rival's passing: dying would boost his reputation and sales.

clue.text: Responsibility has eluded you just lately, by all conclusions

indicators.note: take the conclusion, the final letter, of each word in turn

explanation.surface: A responsibility that has lately been escaping you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' links; last letters of eluded you just lately.
explanation.definitionFit: A duty is an obligation, something one is bound to do.

clue.text: Book that made me laugh reaching middle of epitaph

parts.note: LOL is text-speak for laughing out loud

indicators.note: takes the central letters of the word

explanation.surface: A book whose epitaph had me laughing.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle three letters of epITAph give ITA.
explanation.definitionFit: Lolita is Nabokov's 1955 novel.

clue.text: Writer attributing habit to president

parts.note: Harry Truman was a US president
a capote is a long hooded cloak, a habit

explanation.surface: A writer giving a garment to a president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attributing ... to' is a link joining the two names. Capote is a rare word for a long hooded cloak, a kind of habit.
explanation.definitionFit: Truman Capote was the American author of In Cold Blood.
